answers:

Highlighted the selected passage on page 3.
In Figure 1, the encoder (left) reads the input through six layers. Self-attention lets each word gather context from other input words. A small neural network then processes each position separately, building a richer representation.
The decoder (right) generates output one word at a time through six layers. It attends to earlier output words and the encoder’s representations, then predicts the next word. Positional encodings tell both sides about word order.
Masked attention blocks access to future output words. During training, the full correct answer is available; without masking, the decoder could peek ahead. Masking makes training match generation, when only previously generated words are known.
